Company Description

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design.

As part of the global research organization, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models and Gen AI, Human-AI Collaboration and Trustworthy AI, AI for Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Autonomous Systems, AI Systems Engineering, and Industry AI. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AI solutions to enable inspiring user experiences for Bosch products and services in application areas such as ADAS, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, healthcare, smart home, and building solutions.

Originating from Bosch AI research in Silicon Valley, our Agentic AI Research Group advances cutting-edge research in large language models (LLMs), AI agents, and intelligent autonomous systems. Our research spans autonomous and multi-agent systems, agent reasoning and planning, agent memory, self-improvement, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), reinforcement learning, and multimodal foundation models. We aim to develop novel algorithms and systems that enable AI agents to reason, learn, collaborate, and act effectively in complex real-world environments. We actively collaborate with leading researchers and organizations across academia and industry to advance the state of the art in Agentic AI. Our work regularly contributes to internationally renowned conferences and journals, including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, COLM, and TMLR.

Job Description

You will work on cutting-edge Agentic AI research while tackling real-world challenges in domains such as Industrial AI, Manufacturing, Mobility, and Smart Home. Unlike purely academic environments, you will have the opportunity to develop and validate novel AI technologies on large-scale real-world applications with measurable impact.

You will work closely with experienced Bosch researchers in Silicon Valley and across our global research network, receive mentorship from leading AI experts, and help transform cutting-edge research into real-world AI systems deployed in industrial domains.

Responsibilities

Depending on your expertise and interests, you will contribute to one or more cutting-edge research topics, including:



- Agent systems for industrial applications
- Autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems
- Agent reasoning, planning, and decision making
- Agent memory and long-horizon task execution
- Agent self-improvement, continual learning, and adaptation
- Tool use, function calling, and agent-environment interaction
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Agentic RAG
- Knowledge integration and grounding for agents
- LLM post-training, reinforcement learning, and test-time scaling
- Multi-modal agents leveraging language, vision, and structured data
- Human-agent collaboration and interactive AI systems
- Agent evaluation, benchmarking, reliability, and safety

Key Responsibilities Include



- Conduct novel research in Agentic AI, LLMs, and related fields.
- Design, implement, and evaluate research prototypes demonstrating innovative AI agent capabilities.
- Collaborate closely with Bosch researchers and domain experts to address challenging industrial problems.
- Analyze experimental results and identify opportunities for scientific innovation.
- Publish research outcomes in top-tier AI conferences and journals, such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, and COLM.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications



- Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. or Master's program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field.
- Strong research background in Agentic AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), machine learning, natural language processing, or related areas.
- Experience developing AI agents using modern frameworks and ecosystems
- Strong programming skills in Python and experience with modern AI/ML framework
- Familiarity with agent workflows involves tool use, function calling, retrieval, memory, and multi-step reasoning.
- Experience conducting independent research, designing experiments, and analyzing results.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to work effectively in a collaborative research environment.
- Minimum GPA of 3.0

Preferred Qualifications



- Publication record in top-tier AI, NLP, or machine learning venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, AAAI, COLM).
- Research experience in LLM-based agents, agent architecture, task planning, reasoning, and autonomous decision making.
- Research experience in agent optimization, including post-training, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and self-improvement.
- Experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic retrieval systems, and knowledge-grounded agents.
- Experience with multi-agent systems, agent collaboration, and distributed agent workflows.
- Experience with multi-modal foundation models involving language, vision, and structured data.
- Experience in reinforcement learning, online learning, or adaptive decision-making systems.
- Experience with agent benchmarking, evaluation methodologies, reliability, safety, or alignment.
- Experience in applying Agentic AI technologies to real-world domains such as engineering design, or industrial automation.
- Open-source contributions or demonstrated leadership in AI research communities.

Additional Information

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans 



- Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date.

BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics)



- FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)
- AWIM (A World In Motion)

The U.S. base salary range for this intern position is $53.00-70.00 hourly. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.

For more information on our culture and benefits, please visit:

Culture and Benefits | Bosch in the USA

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

Our interns are integral parts of our teams at TELUS Digital. To help retain our deep culture of collaboration, our interns maintain an in-office presence in a hybrid capacity (Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays on-site). This role is located in Vancouver, BC.

The Opportunity

We believe the best ideas come from shared creativity. What sets us apart from other agencies is that our engineers sit right beside researchers and creatives, so perspectives from multiple disciplines shape our products. Our summer internship program gives current students the chance to make an impact by contributing ideas and adding a fresh perspective to real client projects, all while receiving one-on-one mentoring from our full-time team members. Not only that, but you’ll have snacks galore, and plenty of chances to socialize with your fellow interns — including fun outings during work hours. You'll with us full-time (think 40 hours a week for approx. 16 weeks) and yes, it is definitely paid. Not a bad gig, right?

We understand our responsibility to create a diverse, equitable, and inclusive place within the tech industry, while pushing to make our industry more representative. Because of this responsibility, we need candidates who value diversity and inclusion through their work, team collaboration, or involvement in student organizations.

Your Impact



- Your day-to-day contributions will support real client work, helping TELUS Digital deliver technical excellence for the stakeholders who depend on us
- You’ll have the opportunity to learn every day from engineering leadership
- You’ll build amazing products people love
- You’ll participate in the delivery of large and complex software projects in a team-based environment

Your Background



- You plan to graduate in December 2027 or later
- Have experience with mobile or web development (Swift, Java, Kotlin, TypeScript, Javascript, etc.)
- You’ve done a mobile or web project in school, at a previous internship, or in your spare time
- You have experience integrating AI technology into your development process
- You're a self-starter who embraces new technologies
- You're intellectually curious and enjoy digging into what makes each platform unique
- You are committed to delivering quality code for best-in-class digital experiences
- You appreciate good design and have an eye for details

P.S. Even if you don’t have expertise in all of the qualifications listed, we value new perspectives and encourage you to apply. We’re committed to building a diverse company that reflects the diversity of our users. If you feel confident about a good amount of the bullet points above, we’ll ramp you up on the rest.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

role: ProFound Therapeutics: AI/ML Engineering - SAGE Platform Co-Op
jd:
This position is open exclusively to current Northeastern University Co-Op students.

Location: Watertown, MA 
Work Period: January 2027 to June 2027. This is a full - time, 40 hours per week position with hybrid schedule. 

 About ProFound Therapeutics 

 ProFound ™ Therapeutics is a biotechnology company discovering novel proteins across the expanded human proteome to unlock first-in-class medicines and transformative drug targets. The company’s proprietary   ProFoundry ™ Platform integrates state-of-the-art protein detection, validation, and computational technologies to systematically identify and characterize previously inaccessible proteins and validate their therapeutic potential. This approach has generated a rapidly expanding portfolio of novel targets and drug discovery programs advancing toward the clinic, enabled by strategic collaborations with leading pharmaceutical partners. Together, these efforts support the development of breakthrough treatments across a broad range of disease areas. 

 The company is now poised to define the disease-relevant function of these proteins at scale using advanced proteomics technologies, high throughput experimental biology, and causal agentic AI, enabling rapid identification and characterization of the most promising protein drugs and drug targets. 

 Founded by Flagship Pioneering,   ProFound   works with pharmaceutical partners including Novartis, Pfizer and GSK, and with the Gates Foundation, which has committed up to $35 million to a   ProFound program focused on preeclampsia.

 About Flagship Pioneering 

 ProFound Therapeutics was founded by Flagship Pioneering's venture creation engine that invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health or sustainability. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated and fostered more than 100 scientific ventures, resulting in more than $90 billion in aggregate value. Many of the company’s Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture. Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com .

 Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program 

 Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps. You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions , a dedicated professional development track , and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. By the end, you will carry on a meaningful project outcome , a genuine network , and a front-row view of how Flagship pioneer new ventures that change the world. 

 Position Summary 

 ProFound’s AI/ML team builds SAGE, an internal multi-agent LLM platform that helps our scientists reason over knowledge graphs, biological databases and the scientific literature. SAGE is a central part of how ProFound applies agentic AI to understand novel proteins and accelerate drug discovery. 

 As an AI/ML Engineering Co-Op, you will help extend what SAGE can do and make sure it performs reliably. You will own real features from design through deployment, working closely with our ML engineers and with the scientists who use SAGE every day. The Co-Op is designed to complement your academic training with hands-on experience building and operating a production AI system in an industry drug discovery setting.

 Scope 

• Agent tools and integrations, including external data sources, MCP servers and user-uploaded documents 

• User experience and collaboration features in the SAGE chat interface 

• LLM evaluation and benchmarking (answer quality, accuracy and hallucination rate) 

• Monitoring of usage, performance and cost, and quality checks in CI/CD 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following. 

• Tools and capabilities 

• Design, build and ship new SAGE tools that connect the agent to external data sources, APIs and MCP servers. 

• Extend SAGE’s ability to ingest and reason over documents that users upload, including parsing, chunking and retrieval. 

• Contribute to agent orchestration and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) components that work across knowledge graphs, biological databases and the scientific literature. 

• User experience 

• Build features that make the SAGE chat interface easier to use and collaborate in (e.g., sharing conversations, displaying sources and citations). 

• Gather feedback directly from scientists and turn it into practical, prioritized improvements.

• Evaluation and quality 

• Develop evaluation and benchmarking pipelines that measure SAGE’s answer quality, accuracy and hallucination rate. 

• Help build and curate benchmark datasets with input from scientists, using automated (e.g., LLM-as-judge) and human-review approaches. 

• Help integrate automated quality checks and regression tests into our CI/CD pipeline. 

• Monitoring and engineering practice 

• Build monitoring for SAGE usage, performance, reliability and LLM cost. 

• Write clean, tested and documented code, and take part in code reviews. 

• Present progress and results to the AI/ML team and scientific stakeholders, including a final co-op presentation. 

 What Success Looks Like by the End of the Co-Op 

• At least one new SAGE capability designed, built and deployed to production, and in use by scientists. 

• An evaluation and benchmarking pipeline running regularly, giving the team a clear baseline for answer quality and hallucination rate. 

• Better visibility into SAGE usage, performance and cost. 

• Well-documented work that the team can maintain and build on after the co-op ends. 

 Qualifications 

 Required 

• Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related field, and available for a full-time, 4–6 month co-op term. 

• Strong Python skills. 

• Hands-on experience building with LLMs (e.g., LLM APIs, RAG, agents, or MCP) through coursework, projects, or prior internships 

• Familiarity with Git and software engineering best practices, such as testing, code review and documentation. 

• Curious and self-driven, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical colleagues. 

 Preferred 

• Experience with web or backend development (e.g., FastAPI, React or TypeScript). 

• Experience with LLM evaluation frameworks or observability and tracing tools. 

• Exposure to knowledge graphs, vector databases, or scientific and biological data sources. 

• Familiarity with cloud environments (e.g., AWS), containers (e.g., Docker) and CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions). 

• Prior internship or co-op experience in software or ML engineering. 

• Interest in biology or drug discovery; no biology background required. 

 Why Join Us? 

 You’ll work on a production AI platform used by real scientists. You’ll own projects end to end, with mentorship from experienced ML engineers, and contribute to the discovery of new medicines. 

 What We Offer 

• Build alongside founders. You’ll work inside the same hypothesis-driven process Flagship uses to conceive and launch first-in-category companies. 

• This can be the start of a longer story. Strong co-ops are considered for future opportunities across Flagship and its portfolio companies, not just for this one role. 

• Work alongside people who left the safe path . Your colleagues are scientists, engineers, and operators who chose to build something new rather than join something already established. 

• Take on real ownership. You're contributing to ventures that are still being defined. Your work can shape real decisions, not just support them. 

• Be paid like the contributor you are. Compensation reflects the real work you take on. 
 
 Flagship Pioneering is committed to  equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

 The pay range for this role is $25 - $35 per hour. This role is a short-term engagement that is not eligible for health and welfare benefits. Retirement benefits may be available after completing a set number of hours. Compensation and benefits information is based on ProFound 's good faith estimate as of the date of publication and may be modified in the future.

 Privacy Notice for Applicants: When you apply for a role at Flagship Pioneering, we collect and use personal information you provide (such as your name, contact details, work history, and application materials) to evaluate your application, communicate with you, and comply with legal obligations. Your application data is processed through Greenhouse, our applicant tracking system, and may also be reviewed using AI-assisted screening tools. We do not sell your personal information. California residents have rights under the CCPA/CPRA including to know, delete, and opt out of the sharing of their personal information. If you are located in the EU or UK, we process your data under GDPR and you have rights to access, rectify, and erase your data. To exercise your rights or for questions, contact privacy@flagshippioneering.com.
fit_why: Strong LLM/RAG and Python fit; Python-heavy AI co-op, backend a bonus

 Position Summary 

 As a Bioinformatics Data Engineering Co-Op, you’ll work on production pipelines and datasets, with code review and mentorship from the team. You’ll own a scoped project from start to finish and present it to the team at the end. Typical projects include a QC dashboard, a pipeline benchmark, a new annotation resource or a statistics module. You’ll also work directly with the scientists who use what you build. 

 The Co-Op is designed to complement your academic training with hands-on experience in production bioinformatics and data engineering in an industry drug discovery setting. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following. 

• Run and monitor pipelines. Run Nextflow pipelines for ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), long-read sequencing and DIA proteomics on AWS Batch. Triage failed jobs and summarize QC with MultiQC and alignment metrics. 

• Build and validate QC.   Flag samples that fail set thresholds. Compare results across GENCODE versions. Write automated checks that catch suspicious or missing experiment data before it reaches downstream scoring. 

• Analyze proteomics evidence.   This includes peptide-to-protein mapping, sequence coverage, FDR-filtered evidence, and comparisons across search engines and experiments. 

• Write and test scripts.   Use Python and R to parse, filter and summarize outputs (FASTA, GTF, BAM, peptide and protein tables) into Parquet or TSV. Turn exploratory notebooks into reusable, version-controlled code. 

• Grow the data catalog.   Add or update a dataset: ingest it, document its schema and check it with Athena (SQL) queries. 

• Build tools for scientists.   Prototype a visualization or dashboard (Plotly/Dash, Streamlit or a notebook) that scientists use to review targets and QC results. 

• Document and share.   Write READMEs and runbooks, and present results in team meetings, including a final co-op presentation. 

 Example Projects 

• Benchmark two MS search engines on the same dataset and report where they agree and where they disagree. 

• Build a Ribo-seq QC report that flags samples failing periodicity or mapping thresholds. 

• Add a new QC view to a scientist-facing dashboard, from requirements through deployment. 

• Ingest and document a new biological annotation resource in the data catalog. 

 Qualifications 

 Required 

• Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Biology, Biochemistry, Computer Science or a related field, and available for a full-time, 4–6 month co-op term. 

• Python (pandas) and comfort with the Linux command line. 

• Git, and a habit of writing clear, tested, reproducible code. 

• Coursework or project experience in genomics or molecular biology, such as RNA-seq, translation, protein or DNA sequence analysis, or proteomics basics. 

• Clear written communication; you document what you build. 

 Preferred 

• Basic R. 

• SQL. 

• Nextflow, Snakemake, Airflow or another workflow manager, plus Docker. 

• Exposure to AWS (e.g., S3, EC2, Athena). 

• Familiarity with Ribo-seq, long-read sequencing or mass spectrometry data (e.g., peptides, PSMs, database search). 

• Basic statistics, such as differential expression, false discovery rate and multiple-testing correction. 

• A dashboard or web app you’ve built (e.g., Dash, Streamlit, Shiny), linked from GitHub or a portfolio. 

• Experience with AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) on real projects, with a sense of where they help and where they fail. 

• Exposure to LLM APIs, agents, MCP, or classic ML (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch) applied to biological data. 

 What You’ll Learn and Gain 

• How production Nextflow pipelines are built, tested and run on the cloud. 

• How a data catalog (Glue, Athena, Parquet) turns raw omics outputs into queryable resources. 

• How a computational team supports a drug discovery platform, with exposure to the wet-lab work behind the data. 

• How to use AI-assisted development responsibly in a regulated, data-sensitive setting: verification, testing, and knowing what data may and may not go to which tools. 

• A shipped project with your name on it.

jd:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



Developer Interfaces builds the tools developers and AI agents use to work with 1Password from code. We own the 1Password CLI and we are building out the SDKs and the public developer API experience. Our goal is to make every one of those surfaces feel like one product that is fast, consistent and secure by default. The work sits where developer experience meets security, so the problems are real and the bar for correctness is high.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada/US. This position will be for 4 months - January to April 2027.



What You Can Expect:

 - Ship features and fixes in the 1Password CLI, written in Go and Rust, that developers use every day in terminals, scripts and CI pipelines.

 - Measure and improve CLI and SDK performance with benchmarks and usage data.

 - Write a short design doc before you build, get feedback from senior engineers, then carry the work through code review, testing and release.

 - Learn how a security company builds developer tools, from authentication flows like OAuth to handling secrets safely.

 - Use AI coding tools with judgment. You review and verify what they produce, and you own every line you submit.



What we're looking for:

 - Confidence: A willingness to take on new challenges, and see them through to completion.

 - Humility: You're not afraid to ask "stupid" questions and make mistakes (as long as you learn from them).

 - Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

 - Teamwork: We work together, and succeed as a team!



Bonus points for:

 - Experience with Go or Rust

 - You built a CLI, library or API that other people actually used

 - Familiarity with OAuth 2.0 or other authentication flows

 - Experience with developer docs, OpenAPI specs or static site generators

 - Interest in how AI agents use developer tools
   
   

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of most roles. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events. 


How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



You’ll join our Credential Brokering team. We build and scale our newest platform that enables granular access for humans, agents and machines. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to the early stages of this new platform while it’s rapidly gaining traction. You’ll build reliable credential infrastructure that empowers all major runtimes, and help keep people in control of their access while they adopt AI.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada/US. This position will be for 4 months - January to April 2027.



What You Can Expect:

 - You’ll participate in the entire software lifecycle and have opportunities to contribute ideas, build PoCs, take user- and partner feedback for our platform, and ship features and improvements in production.
   
   - Participate in the entire software development lifecycle.
   
   - Contribute ideas and build proofs of concept (PoCs).
   
   - Incorporate user and partner feedback into our platform.
   
   - Ship features and improvements to production.



What we're looking for:

 - Confidence: A willingness to take on new challenges, and see them through to completion.

 - Humility: You're not afraid to ask "stupid" questions and make mistakes (as long as you learn from them).

 - Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

 - Teamwork: We work together, and succeed as a team!



Bonus points for:

 - Back end development experience with Go or Rust.

 - Experience building developer interfaces and platforms; APIs enabling your developer customers to build new products on top.
   
   

Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of most roles. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events. 


How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

jd:
Coretek is at the forefront of innovation, providing a broad range of AI, Security, and Managed Services designed to help businesses improve operational efficiency and drive growth. We are seeking AI & Automation Interns who are passionate about artificial intelligence, automation, and applying emerging technologies to real-world business challenges.
 Coretek’s AI & Data Co-Op Program places you on a team that applies AI, alongside automation, to build solutions used by employees across the business. Interns work directly with the teams who will use each solution to understand their needs, optimize workflows and operational processes, and apply AI models, automation technologies, and other tools to solve real business problems. Projects are refined through hands-on testing, feedback, and iteration until solutions are stable, reliable, and capable of operating independently.
 This role provides hands-on experience across the Microsoft AI and automation ecosystem, including Azure AI, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power BI, Microsoft Teams, and Salesforce, while giving interns exposure to the full lifecycle of developing and deploying AI-powered business solutions in a consulting environment.
 Responsibilities: 
 
• Partner with business stakeholders across different departments to identify processes suited to automation and scope solutions around their needs.  
• Design, build, and refine automation and AI-agent solutions, progressing from an initial prototype to a stable, deployable solution.  
• Apply AI techniques, such as generative AI models, prompt design, and conversational agents, to automate and improve business processes.  
• Test and validate solutions against real data and edge cases, addressing inaccuracies in AI output before deployment.  
• Communicate technical work to non-technical stakeholders, including estimating and reporting the time or effort a solution saves.  
• Document workflows, architecture, and design decisions clearly enough for others to maintain, extend, or take over the solution.  
• Collaborate with other interns and team members to share ideas and troubleshoot challenges in a fast-paced, evolving environment.  
• Research emerging AI and automation technologies and share relevant findings with the team.

Requirements 
 
• Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Business Administration (Technology & Operations), Information Systems, or a related field.  
• Basic understanding of AI concepts and frameworks (e.g., large language models, Azure AI, Copilot Studio).  
• Comfortable working through ambiguity, developing a solution iteratively as requirements and constraints become clearer.  
• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, particularly when working with financial, sales, or client-facing data.  
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams with varying technical backgrounds.  
• Self-motivated, with the ability to own a project from prototype through testing, documentation, and deployment.  
• Ability to manage multiple tasks and adapt to shifting priorities in a dynamic environment.  
• Exposure to automation platforms (e.g., Power Automate, UiPath, Automation Anywhere), Microsoft Cloud (e.g., Azure, Copilot Studio), or programming languages such as Python, C#, or Java is a plus.  
• Power usage of coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) is a plus. 
 Hires who succeed in this role treat measurable impact, such as time or effort saved, as a core part of the solution design, not an afterthought. They work persistently through the iteration required to improve AI accuracy, and document their work thoroughly enough that it remains useful after their internship ends.
